page: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is a dedicated CPU virtual server instance running on the QEMU hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB per core, and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the ccx13 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested instances via stress-ng. However, its multi-core capabilities are limited, scoring in the bottom 25% for multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests due to its 2-vCPU constraint. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; read-only small-block memory bandwidth and Passmark memory scores fall into the bottom 10%, while large-block write bandwidth is average. Real-world application benchmarks show average performance for single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, but weak performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation, the ccx13 offers predictable compute performance without the risk of noisy-neighbor resource contention common in shared-core environments. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring consistent single-threaded execution rather than massive parallel processing. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, small-scale web serving, single-threaded background workers, and basic text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high memory bandwidth or extensive multi-core scaling.
